input.hypothesis: Democrats take the House in the 2026 midterms

nodes.statement: Democrats win a House majority in the 2026 midterms
nodes.resolution: Associated Press calls enough House races for a Democratic majority
nodes.rationale: A narrow national environment makes turnout and a small number of suburban districts decisive.
assumptions: The number of competitive districts remains near current estimates

nodes.statement: Suburban turnout exceeds 2022 levels in competitive districts
nodes.resolution: Certified turnout in targeted suburban counties exceeds the 2022 share
nodes.rationale: College-educated suburban turnout has been the most consistent margin driver in close House races.
assumptions: Turnout operations remain funded through Election Day

nodes.statement: Unemployment remains below 4.5 percent into the election
nodes.resolution: The October employment report shows unemployment below 4.5 percent
nodes.rationale: A stable labor market reduces the penalty typically borne by the incumbent party.
assumptions: A recession does not begin before October

nodes.statement: Democrats field credible candidates in most open suburban seats
nodes.resolution: Party filings show candidates with prior elected or military experience in targeted seats
nodes.rationale: Candidate quality matters disproportionately where partisan registration is nearly balanced.
assumptions: Primary contests do not nominate unelectable outliers

nodes.statement: Headline inflation reaccelerates above 3.5 percent before Election Day
nodes.resolution: Three-month annualized headline CPI exceeds 3.5 percent
nodes.rationale: A visible cost-of-living shock changes the retrospective economic vote faster than policy messaging can.
assumptions: Energy and shelter inflation rise together

nodes.statement: A Democratic House prioritizes drug-pricing oversight hearings
nodes.resolution: The incoming committee agenda lists drug-pricing oversight as a first-quarter priority
nodes.rationale: A majority shift changes committee subpoena and hearing priorities even without Senate control.
assumptions: Leadership assigns health policy to a high-profile committee

nodes.name: S&P 500 ETF
nodes.rationale: The broad index reflects the macro outcome more than a single congressional result.
assumptions: Monetary policy remains the dominant market driver

nodes.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR
nodes.rationale: Managed-care and pharma valuations are sensitive to oversight and reimbursement headlines.
assumptions: Sector earnings remain otherwise on guidance

edges.mechanism: Higher participation improves margins in marginal suburban districts
A stable labor market limits the incumbent-party economic penalty
Stronger challengers convert national sentiment into individual-seat wins
A renewed inflation shock weakens the incumbent economic case
Committee control sets the oversight calendar
A stable employment backdrop supports earnings multiples
Higher inflation raises discount-rate and margin concerns
Oversight risk modestly discounts health-care policy-sensitive names
Broad risk appetite transmits into the defensive sector

summary.headline: The House outcome rests on suburban turnout and inflation, while the market effect is more sector-specific than index-wide.
summary.mainUncertainty: Whether late inflation changes the national vote enough to outweigh candidate quality.
